slides.heading: Linked List Construction
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Linked Lists
slides.narration: Let's solve Linked List Construction, a medium linked lists problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Doubly linked list with head/tail supporting setHead, setTail, insertBefore, insertAfter, insertAtPosition (1-based), removeNodesWithValue, remove and containsNodeWithValue.
Inserting a node already in the list moves it.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Doubly linked list with head or tail supporting setHead, setTail, insertBefore, insertAfter, insertAtPosition (1-based), removeNodesWithValue, remove and containsNodeWithValue. Inserting a node already in the list moves it.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: A doubly linked list keeps head and tail pointers so most operations rewire a few links.
slides.narration: A doubly linked list keeps head and tail pointers so most operations rewire a few links.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Singly linked → removing needs the previous node (O(n))
Doubly linked: O(1) insert/remove given a node
slides.narration: With a singly linked list, removing a node needs its predecessor, which means a scan. Doubly linked nodes know both neighbours, so inserting and removing a known node is constant time.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. Remove a node from its spot before reinserting
2. Update head and tail on the edges
3. Walk for position and value ops
slides.narration: Step by step. First, remove a node from its spot before reinserting. Second, update head and tail on the edges. Third, walk for position and value ops.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: setHead(1)
slides.narration: Set head to one: the list was empty, so one is both head and tail.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: setTail(4)
slides.narration: Set tail to four: insert after the current tail.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: insertBefore(4, 3)
slides.narration: Insert three before four: rewire three's prev to one and next to four, then fix both neighbours.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: insertAtPosition(2, 2)
slides.narration: Insert two at position two, walking from the head to the node currently there.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: removeNodesWithValue(3)
slides.narration: Remove nodes with value three: unlink by connecting its prev and next, and clear its pointers.

slides.heading: Java solution (1/4)
slides.narration: Set head and set tail handle the empty case and otherwise delegate to insert before or after. Insert before removes the node, wires its prev and next, and updates either head or the previous node's next.

slides.heading: Complexity
bullets: Time: O(1) for head/tail/insertBefore/After/remove, O(n) for position/value ops
slides.narration: Time is constant for head or tail or insertBefore or After or remove, O of n for position or value ops. Space is constant.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Inserting a node already in the list: remove it first
Update head/tail when touching the ends
slides.narration: If the node being inserted is already in the list, remove it first. Always update head and tail when operating at the ends.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
slides.narration: Draw the pointer changes before coding. This structure is the backbone of an LRU cache.
